title: Emberly Connect renewal + EU/APAC expansion sync
summary: Check-in to align on renewal timing, capacity uplift for Q4 traffic growth, and adding EU + APAC regions. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, data residency concerns, SOC2/KMS questions, and next steps for pricing and pilot benchmarks. Agreed to a 6-month commitment amendment with staged capacity increases; Redwood to send revised quote and schedule private pilot for EU region.
topics: Adding EU and APAC regions (VPC/private serving options)
Security: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML
Pricing model for burst vs reserved capacity
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-06-16
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Daniel Park, Sofia Ruiz, Marcus Hale (Redwood); Maya Singh, Tom Brenner, Irene Kwan, Liam O'Connor (Emberly)

Auto-generated summary: follow-up on renewal + regional expansion (may contain errors).

[00:00] Daniel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to the 50 minute window. I'm Daniel from Redwood, AE, with Sofia our SE and Marcus on CSM. Maya?
[00:12] Maya: Hi, hi, thanks. Quick note, we had a leadership sync earlier so trying to move fast — timeline is end of Q3 for new regions ideally.
[00:18] Daniel: Great. The agenda is renewal terms, capacity uplift numbers you gave last week, and the EU/APAC onramp approach.
[00:26] Tom: Right, we bumped projections — about 2.5x tokens and around 3x concurrent sessions during peak.
[00:34] Sofia: Got it. Do you mean concurrent API connections or user sessions?
[00:38] Tom: Mostly API concurrency from our chat layer. Users map to sessions but it's the concurrent requests that matter.
[00:44] Sofia: Okay that's helpful, it affects batching and cache footprint.
[00:48] Irene: On security, we need clarity on data residency — logs, KV cache, and whether PII can be excluded from Red wood's hosted logs.
[00:58] Marcus: Yep, we covered this in the security pack — we can provide options: Hosted with regional isolation, Dedicated reserved pools, or Private VPC for full control.
[01:08] Liam: Cost question up front: if we go EU+APAC, how does that change unit pricing? We have procurement constraints.
[01:16] Daniel: Good call. There are two levers — region routing/egress costs and capacity commit. Reserved capacity across regions reduces unit costs; burst is higher. We'll send an amendment with per-region pricing.
[01:26] Maya: Are there SLA differences if we use Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[01:30] Sofia: Slight differences —Dedicated gets an SLA for throughput and lower tail latency guarantees. Private gives you customer-managed infra so SLAs depend on the deployment template but we support audit hooks and fallbacks. Hosted is fastest to spin up but shared infra.
[01:44] Tom: For latency targets, our product needs 95th percentile under 150ms for short prompts in EU. Can Redwood meet that from a hosted EU region?
[01:54] Sofia: For the models you're using, yes we can hit that in our EU region with proper placement and caching; we'll likely recommend prefix KV caching and smaller batch windows for low-latency paths. If you need stricter tails, Dedicated in-region reduces variability.
[02:06] Maya: Understood. Also legal asked about KMS / HSM integrations — they want to know if keys can stay in our cloud KMS.
[02:14] Marcus: You can bring your own key via KMS integration on Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports envelope encryption with our managed keys and we can enable customer KMS for enterprise tiers.
[02:24] Irene: Can we get a short write-up of the KMS flow? We had a question whether token caching is encrypted server-side in a way we can audit.
[02:32] Daniel: Absolutely — we'll share the KMS diagram and SOC 2 artifacts. We'll note KV cache encryption and audit log fields.
[02:38] Tom: Cool. On capacity, we wanted a staged uplift: +50% in Sept, +2x in Nov, full 2.5x in Jan. Is that a pattern Redwood supports in a single contract?
[02:50] Daniel: Yes, we can do staged ramping inside the commitment. We usually propose a base reserved capacity and a schedule for committed increments with pre-agreed pricing.
[02:58] Liam: For procurement — we need the pricing by next Tuesday to review finance.
[03:02] Daniel: We'll get that out Monday, latest.

[03:10] [break — 1 min background noise] 
[03:40] Maya: One more technical: if we do EU private deployment, what parts of the control plane remain with Redwood? We need to confirm no customer data leaves region.
[03:50] Sofia: In Private mode the control plane is split: the customer has a private control plane option where metadata and model pins are controlled by you; logs and tokens can be kept in-region. There are still telemetry signals we can optionally route off for support, but that can be disabled.
[04:04] Irene: Okay, good. Audit logs are critical — can they be exported to our SIEM (Splunk) with guaranteed retention 1 year?
[04:12] Marcus: Yes, we can push audit logs to your collector over TLS and you can define retention. We'll include fields and sample event types in the security doc.
[04:20] Tom: There was also an earlier note about GPU types — in APAC we prefer A10G equivalent or newer. Is that configurable for Dedicated?
[04:28] Sofia: For Dedicated yes, you can request specific hardware classes for a pool. For Hosted we choose optimal instances but we can prioritize certain families for your account with some lead time.
[04:38] Maya: Are there any blockers for setting up a private pilot in EU? We want to run 2k concurrent sessions and do latency checks.
[04:46] Sofia: We can spin a pilot cluster in EU with the Dedicated pool replica — timeline ~3 weeks for provisioning and smoke tests.
[04:54] Liam: Who signs off on the pilot cost? We need an internal PO for staging.
[04:58] Daniel: We'll attach a pilot quote. Usually a smaller short-term commitment or trial credits can cover that.

[05:06] [05:06] Daniel: Quick competitive note — we know you evaluated some other vendors; did anything important come up?
[05:12] Maya: Yeah — one vendor, Anthropic's hosting partner, offered regional private clouds but their telemetry story was weak. We also looked at Replicate for self-hosting but had ops concerns.
[05:22] Tom: Also considered OpenAI for embeddings but cost at scale is problematic.

[05:26] Sofia: Noted. We'll emphasize our observability and cost controls — token-level cost breakdowns and per-route tracing.
[05:34] Irene: About compliance, can we get SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts?
[05:38] Marcus: Yes, we will share redacted SOC2 Type II report, and ISO attestation. We'll also include our penetration test summary.

[05:46] Maya: Okay we need to firm up the term. Leadership prefers a 6–12 month extension rather than month-to-month. If we do 6 months with staged capacity, can we lock pricing?
[05:56] Daniel: Yes, we can lock pricing for the committed period and bake in an option to renew at pre-negotiated rates.

[06:02] [longer stretch — ambient talking] 
[06:20] Tom: For the routing policy, we want primary EU and fallback to US with region-aware keys. Can Redwood support model variant fallback automatically?
[06:30] Sofia: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants and we can pin versions per region. We'll propose a routing policy that prefers local region and falls back with a rate limit to prevent spikes.

[06:42] Maya: Any details on data residency for embeddings? We do PII redaction in-app but logs might still include embeddings.
[06:52] Marcus: Embeddings are treated as data objects — you can choose to keep embeddings in-region or replicate. For privacy, we recommend in-region storage and endpoint-level RBAC so only the app service account can access them.

[07:04] Irene: Will RBAC integrate with our SSO (SAML + SCIM)?
[07:08] Sofia: Yes, SSO SAML and SCIM provisioning supported. We'll include sample SAML metadata.

[07:14] [quick QA back-and-forth] 
[07:36] Liam: Procurement wants the amendment language about early termination if we don't hit adoption targets. Can Redwood accommodate a ramp clause?
[07:44] Daniel: We can add a ramp clause with scaled billing if usage doesn't reach the planned thresholds; details in the contract team will draft.

[07:52] Marcus: To summarize the concrete asks so far: 1) Revised quote with staged capacity and per-region prices; 2) SOC2/ISO/KMS flow docs; 3) Pilot plan for EU with timeline and hardware options; 4) Contract amendment template with ramp clause.
[08:06] Maya: Yes exactly. Also, sample audit log schema for Splunk integration.

[08:12] Sofia: We'll package those and send by Monday.

[08:18] [small side conversation — coordinating calendars] 

[08:40] Tom: One more technical item — we might need a quantized model for APAC to save cost. Does Redwood support mixed quantization across pools?
[08:50] Sofia: Yes, you can run different quantization profiles per pool; runtime will pick compatible kernels. We'll recommend profiles based on your quality vs cost tradeoff.

[09:02] Maya: Good. For the pilot metrics we'll run: 95p latency, median latency, token cost per 1k, error rate, and model output quality on a few prompt sets.
[09:12] Sofia: Perfect. We'll help define the eval prompts and automate regressions in Redwood Optimize.

[09:20] [transcript jump — mid-call details and clarifications omitted] 

[30:00] Daniel: Circling back — procurement deadlines, Liam?
[30:04] Liam: We need a PO request by June 23 to hit finance cycle.
[30:08] Daniel: Okay we'll prioritize Monday delivery and include a clear PO line with terms.

[36:10] Irene: Any blockers on encryption in transit for the pilot?
[36:14] Sofia: No — TLS + mTLS available for private deployments. We'll include cert rotation notes.

[42:00] Marcus: Action items we captured: pricing, pilot plan, security artifacts.
[42:06] Daniel: Final readout — are there any outstanding risks?
[42:10] Maya: Only one — we need to demo throughput under load, otherwise leadership might push back.
[42:16] Sofia: We'll run benchmark and share the logs with you and a readout call.

[50:00] Daniel: Thanks all. We'll send the packet Monday and propose a follow-up check-in next Thursday for legal + procurement.
[50:10] Maya: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript (auto-gen may contain errors).
